advances:
The registered uniform-simplex assertion is equivalent to an exact scalar
assertion about the concave \(d\)-th root of the fiber-volume profile.
There is no additional common-body or affine-compatibility restriction:
every scalar concave root has a compact full-dimensional realization by
homothetic \(d\)-simplices for which
\[
M(z)=\gamma_dw_z,
\qquad
\gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
\]
and the same constant affine graph consists of maximal-depth points in
every fiber.  Thus a scalar counterexample is automatically an exact
common-body counterexample, while a proof of the scalar assertion proves
the registered statement for every convex body.
author: research-agent
external_sources:
R. J. Gardner, "The Brunn-Minkowski Inequality," Bulletin of the
American Mathematical Society 39 (2002), 355-405, Theorem 4.1,
DOI 10.1090/S0273-0979-02-00941-2,
https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-02-00941-2.
The exact form used is: for nonempty bounded measurable
\(A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(0<\lambda<1\),
\[
\operatorname{vol}_d((1-\lambda)A+\lambda B)^{1/d}
\geq
(1-\lambda)\operatorname{vol}_d(A)^{1/d}
+\lambda\operatorname{vol}_d(B)^{1/d}.
\]
The statement permits zero-volume inputs.  Here all input sets and their
Minkowski combinations are compact and therefore measurable.

Branko Grünbaum, "Partitions of Mass-Distributions and of Convex Bodies
by Hyperplanes," Pacific Journal of Mathematics 10 (1960), no. 4,
1257-1261, Theorem 2 and its proof in Section 3, pages 1259-1260,
DOI 10.2140/pjm.1960.10.1257,
https://doi.org/10.2140/pjm.1960.10.1257.
The exact form used is: if \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a
\(d\)-dimensional convex body with centroid \(c_K\), then every closed
halfspace \(H\) containing \(c_K\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{vol}_d(K\cap H)
\geq
\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d\operatorname{vol}_d(K).
\]
proof:
1. Every convex body produces a scalar instance.

Let
\[
C\subseteq\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d
\]
be a compact full-dimensional convex body in the registered subgoal.
Write
\[
P:=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbb R^2}(C),
\qquad
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},
\qquad
r_C(z):=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)^{1/d}.
\tag{18}
\]
The base projection \(P\) is compact, convex, and full-dimensional.

For \(z_0,z_1\in P\), \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\), and
\(z_\lambda=(1-\lambda)z_0+\lambda z_1\), convexity gives
\[
(1-\lambda)C_{z_0}+\lambda C_{z_1}
\subseteq C_{z_\lambda}.
\tag{19}
\]
Brunn-Minkowski, including zero-volume sections, gives
\[
r_C(z_\lambda)
\geq
(1-\lambda)r_C(z_0)+\lambda r_C(z_1).
\tag{20}
\]
Thus \(r_C\) is concave.

It is also upper semicontinuous.  Suppose \(z_k\to z\) in \(P\).  All
fibers lie in the fixed compact vertical projection of \(C\).  For every
\(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
C_{z_k}\subseteq C_z+\varepsilon\overline{\mathbb B}_2^d
\tag{21}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\).  Otherwise, compactness would give a
subsequence \(x_k\in C_{z_k}\) converging to a point \(x\) outside the
right side, while closedness of \(C\) would give \((z,x)\in C\), a
contradiction.  Hence
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{z_k})
\leq
\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z+\varepsilon\overline{\mathbb B}_2^d).
\]
The compact parallel sets on the right decrease to \(C_z\) as
\(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).  Continuity from above of Lebesgue measure
therefore yields
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_{z_k})
\leq\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z).
\tag{22}
\]
This proves upper semicontinuity of \(r_C\).

For every \(z\) with \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)>0\), the fiber
\(C_z\) is a \(d\)-dimensional convex body.  Its centroid \(c_z\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\substack{
J\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
c_z\in J}}
\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z\cap J)
\geq
\gamma_dw_z
\tag{23}
\]
by Grünbaum's centroid halfspace theorem.  Consequently its maximal
absolute depth obeys
\[
M_C(z)\geq\gamma_dw_z.
\tag{24}
\]

All scalar hypotheses (3)-(12) are the corresponding registered
hypotheses on these same fiber volumes.  If \((\mathrm S_d)\) gives a
simplex \(T\), then (24) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}T}M_C(v)\,
\kappa(T,z_0)
&\geq
\gamma_d
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}T}w_v\,
\kappa(T,z_0)\\
&\geq\frac W{64}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
\]
Thus the scalar assertion implies the registered assertion for every
body.

2. Every scalar instance has a sharp simplex-fiber realization.

Let \(P,r,z_0\) be any scalar instance.  Choose a \(d\)-simplex
\[
K\subseteq\mathbb R^d
\]
of volume one whose centroid is the origin.  The origin is in the
interior of \(K\).  Its Minkowski functional
\[
p_K(x):=\inf\{\lambda\geq0:x\in\lambda K\}
\tag{26}
\]
is finite, continuous, convex, positively homogeneous, and coercive.
Define
\[
C_r:=
\{(z,x)\in P\times\mathbb R^d:p_K(x)\leq r(z)\}.
\tag{27}
\]

This set is convex.  If \(p_K(x_i)\leq r(z_i)\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_K((1-\lambda)x_0+\lambda x_1)
&\leq
(1-\lambda)p_K(x_0)+\lambda p_K(x_1)\\
&\leq
(1-\lambda)r(z_0)+\lambda r(z_1)\\
&\leq
r((1-\lambda)z_0+\lambda z_1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
Upper semicontinuity of \(r\) makes its hypograph closed, so (27) is
closed.  Compactness of \(P\), boundedness of \(r\), and coercivity of
\(p_K\) make it bounded.  Hence \(C_r\) is compact and convex.

Condition (6) implies that \(D_+\) contains three noncollinear points.
Concavity of \(r\) makes it strictly positive throughout the interior of
their triangle.  Therefore (27) contains an open subset of
\(\mathbb R^{2+d}\), so \(C_r\) is full-dimensional.

Positive homogeneity gives every real fiber exactly:
\[
(C_r)_z=r(z)K
\qquad(z\in P),
\tag{29}
\]
where \(0K=\{0\}\).  Since \(K\) has volume one,
\[
\operatorname{vol}_d((C_r)_z)=r(z)^d.
\tag{30}
\]
Thus the lattice-fiber weights of \(C_r\) are exactly (2).  In
particular, \(D_+\), \(W\), every singleton and primitive-line mass, every
closed base-halfspace mass, \(Q^\circ\), and
\(\mathcal E^\Psi_d(w;z_0)\) are unchanged.  All strict inequalities in
(3), (4), (7), and (12) transfer literally.

3. Exact maximal depth of every simplex fiber.

Let
\[
\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d
\]
be the barycentric coordinate functions of \(K\).  For every \(x\in K\),
some \(i\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_i(x)\geq\frac1{d+1}.
\tag{31}
\]
The set
\[
J_i(x):=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\lambda_i(y)\geq\lambda_i(x)\}
\tag{32}
\]
is a proper closed halfspace containing \(x\).  Its intersection with
\(K\) is a homothetic copy of \(K\) with linear ratio
\(1-\lambda_i(x)\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{vol}_d(K\cap J_i(x))
=(1-\lambda_i(x))^d
\leq
\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d
=\gamma_d.
\tag{33}
\]
No point of \(K\) has absolute depth greater than \(\gamma_d\).

The origin is the centroid of \(K\).  Grünbaum's theorem gives the
opposite inequality for every proper closed halfspace containing the
origin.  Therefore
\[
\max_{x\in K}
\inf_{\substack{
J\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
x\in J}}
\operatorname{vol}_d(K\cap J)
=
\delta_K(0)
=\gamma_d.
\tag{34}
\]
The boundary in (32) is an affine hyperplane and has
\(d\)-dimensional volume zero, so no boundary convention changes
(33)-(34).

An invertible homothety maps proper closed halfspaces bijectively and
multiplies \(d\)-dimensional volumes by the \(d\)-th power of its scale.
Equations (29) and (34) now give, for every \(z\in D_+\),
\[
M_{C_r}(z)
=
\gamma_dr(z)^d
=
\gamma_dw_z.
\tag{35}
\]
If \(r(z)=0\), the fiber is the singleton \(\{0\}\), its
\(d\)-dimensional volume is zero, and every absolute depth is zero.
Thus (35) extends with value zero to all zero-volume fibers.

The origin attains (35) in every fiber.  Consequently the constant map
\[
s:P\longrightarrow\mathbb R^d,
\qquad
s(z):=0,
\tag{36}
\]
is an affine simultaneous maximizer over the entire base projection.
For every \(t\geq0\), if
\[
G_t(C_r):=
\{(z,x)\in C_r:\delta_{C_r}(z,x)\geq t\},
\tag{37}
\]
then
\[
\{(z,0):\gamma_dr(z)^d\geq t\}
\subseteq G_t(C_r).
\tag{38}
\]
The sets \(G_t(C_r)\) are the common depth bundles of this one body.
Their convexity follows directly from Brunn-Minkowski.  Any proper closed
fiber halfspace containing \(x\) contains the parallel
boundary-through-\(x\) halfspace, so absolute depth is the infimum over
boundary-through-point caps indexed by unit normals.  For each fixed
normal, the corresponding cap sections Minkowski-interpolate under convex
combinations of \((z,x)\).  Taking \(d\)-th roots, applying
Brunn-Minkowski, and then taking the infimum over normals proves concavity
of \(\delta_{C_r}^{1/d}\), whose superlevel sets are convex.  Thus the
chosen vertex maximizers \(0\) on every lattice simplex interpolate on the
same constant graph inside the relevant common bundle.

4. Converse and exact equivalence.

Suppose a scalar instance fails (15).  Its realization \(C_r\) satisfies
all registered hypotheses by (30), and (35) gives, for every eligible
rank-zero, rank-one, or rank-two simplex containing \(z_0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}T}M_{C_r}(v)\,
\kappa(T,z_0)
&=
\gamma_d
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}T}w_v\,
\kappa(T,z_0)\\
&<\frac W{64}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{39}
\]
Hence \(C_r\) is an exact common-body counterexample to the registered
statement.  Combined with (25), this proves both directions of the
claimed equivalence.

BOUNDARY, RANK, AND QUANTIFIER AUDIT

* The construction and equivalence hold for every
  \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), with the exact
  \(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\).
* Compactness of \(P\) makes the positive lattice support finite, so every
  sum in (2), (7), and (11) is finite.
* Zero-root fibers are exactly \(\{0\}\), have zero
  \(d\)-volume, and have maximal absolute depth zero.
* Every cap in (23), (32), and (34) is a proper closed halfspace.
  Hyperplane boundaries have zero \(d\)-volume.
* The realization preserves every strict premise exactly, including the
  singleton, primitive-line, parity, and low-energy inequalities.
* The definition of \(\kappa\) is unchanged.  Therefore rank zero, rank
  one, rank two, proper closed relative halfspaces, boundary lattice
  points, and cases in which \(z_0\) lies on a simplex face transfer
  without modification.
* The selector (36) is defined on all of \(P\).  No extension from one
  simplex, gluing of local selectors, or compatibility assumption is
  used.
statement:
Fix \(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) and put
\[
\gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
\tag{1}
\]
Define a scalar instance as follows.  Let
\[
P\subseteq\mathbb R^2
\]
be compact, convex, and full-dimensional, and let
\[
r:P\longrightarrow[0,\infty)
\]
be concave and upper semicontinuous.  For \(z\in\mathbb Z^2\), put
\[
w_z:=
\begin{cases}
r(z)^d,&z\in P,\\
0,&z\notin P,
\end{cases}
\qquad
D_+:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:w_z>0\},
\qquad
W:=\sum_z w_z.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(z_0\in D_+\), assume \(W>0\), and impose the exact scalar
hypotheses of the registered subgoal:
\[
w_z<\frac W4
\qquad(z\in\mathbb Z^2),
\tag{3}
\]
\[
\sum_{z\in(a+L)\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z<\frac W2
\tag{4}
\]
for every coset \(a+L\) of every primitive rank-one sublattice
\(L\leq\mathbb Z^2\),
\[
\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^2}w_z\geq\frac W4
\tag{5}
\]
for every proper closed halfspace \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) containing
\(z_0\),
\[
z_0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}D_+,
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
Q^\circ:=
\sum_{\rho\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2}
\left(\sum_{z\equiv\rho\pmod2}w_z\right)^2
-\sum_z w_z^2
>
\frac{16-e}{256}W^2.
\tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
R_0:=w_{z_0}^{1/d},
\qquad
S_0:=2(1-\gamma_d)^{1/d}R_0,
\tag{8}
\]
\[
\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B):=
A^d+B^d-
\max_{\substack{
0\leq s\leq A,\ 0\leq t\leq B\\
s+t\leq S_0}}
(s^d+t^d),
\tag{9}
\]
\[
\Psi_{d,S_0}(A,B):=
\min\{\Phi_{d,S_0}(A,B),A^d,B^d\},
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
\mathcal E^\Psi_d(w;z_0):=
\gamma_dw_{z_0}
+
\sum_{v/\pm}
\Psi_{d,S_0}\left(
w_{z_0+v}^{1/d},w_{z_0-v}^{1/d}
\right),
\tag{11}
\]
where the sum uses one representative from each
\(\{v,-v\}\subseteq\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\).  Assume
\[
\mathcal E^\Psi_d(w;z_0)<\frac W{64}.
\tag{12}
\]

For \(q\in\{0,1,2\}\), let
\[
v_0,\ldots,v_q\in D_+
\]
be affinely independent, put
\[
T:=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_q\},
\]
and suppose \(z_0\in T\).  If \(q=0\), define
\[
\kappa(T,z_0):=1.
\tag{13}
\]
If \(q>0\), define
\[
\kappa(T,z_0):=
\min_{\substack{
Q\subseteq\operatorname{aff}(T)
\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
z_0\in Q}}
\#(T\cap Q\cap\mathbb Z^2).
\tag{14}
\]

Let \((\mathrm S_d)\) denote the scalar conclusion that some such
rank-at-most-two simplex satisfies
\[
\gamma_d
\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}T}w_v\,
\kappa(T,z_0)
\geq\frac W{64}.
\tag{15}
\]

Then the following universal assertions are equivalent:

1. Every compact full-dimensional convex body
   \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d\) satisfying the hypotheses
   of `n2-low-energy-uniform-simplex` satisfies its registered conclusion.

2. Every scalar instance satisfying (2)-(12) satisfies
   \((\mathrm S_d)\).

More precisely, every scalar instance has an explicit compact
full-dimensional convex-body realization \(C_r\) with exactly the same
weights, support, strict hypotheses, and energy, such that
\[
M_{C_r}(z)=\gamma_dw_z
\tag{16}
\]
for every positive lattice fiber.  The constant map
\[
s(z)\equiv0
\tag{17}
\]
is a simultaneous maximal-depth selector on the entire base projection.
